title: Wikipedians Believed AI Would Come and Go. They Were Wrong
gist: A book excerpt argues AI is an accelerant, not the cause, of Wikipedia's decline: it lost almost a quarter of readership (over 1.1 billion visits a month) since 2022, AI chatbots click through at 0.33 percent versus about 9 percent for Google, and editors are thinning, while the platform banned LLM-written content in March 2026. The author frames this as the end of the encyclopedic age.

themes.theme: AI erodes Wikipedia's traffic and editor base

insights.claim: Since 2022 Wikipedia has lost almost a quarter of its readership, more than 1.1 billion visits a month, presumably to AI summaries, even though Pew counted 1.9 trillion views from 2015 to 2025 (508 million a day).
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Shows AI answer layers cannibalizing human-curated content sources that LLMs themselves depend on.
insights.locator: The Pew Research company marked the occasion

insights.claim: Click-through from AI chatbots to cited sources was only 0.33 percent versus closer to 9 percent for Google search, so AI citations do not return audiences to the sources they draw on.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Low referral rates undermine the traffic and donation or editor funnel for knowledge publishers, a structural issue for the content-licensing debate.
insights.locator: Even when answers offered by AI agents contain links

insights.claim: Wikipedia's model depends on readers becoming editors, so falling readership produces fewer editors doing more work, with no pipeline for expert editors and a risk of becoming a temple maintained by an ageing priesthood.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: A shrinking contributor base threatens quality of the human-written corpus on which AI models train.
insights.quote: a smaller club working harder to maintain something fewer people see

insights.claim: A Wikipedian warned Wikipedia could become a footnote in the training data of models that have moved on, and that paying editors, once sacrilegious, now has to be reconsidered.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Suggests content sources may need compensated-contributor models as AI extracts value, which is relevant to data-licensing economics.
insights.quote: footnote in the training data of models that have moved on without us
insights.locator: Artificial intelligence was an existential risk to Wikipedia

insights.claim: Gen Z economic precarity has trained many to see unpaid labor as a scam, so Wikipedia editing is viewed as thankless work that AI companies strip-mine for profit.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Volunteer-driven knowledge infrastructure faces a motivation shortfall when AI firms capture the value.
insights.quote: Economic precarity [has] trained many Gen Zers to see any unpaid labor as a scam

insights.claim: A Wikipedian argued AI is merely an accelerant of a deeper generational shift, as younger users scroll and consume fragments instead of reading articles, so the encyclopedia form factor may be losing relevance faster than any technology explains.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Attributing traffic decline to format change rather than AI alone cautions against assuming AI is the only disruptor of text media.
insights.quote: AI is an accelerant, not the fire

insights.claim: A Princeton study found about 5 percent of nearly 3,000 new English Wikipedia articles in August 2024 contained substantial AI-generated content, and by March 2026 Wikipedia banned writing with large language models outright, limiting them to translation and minor proofreading.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: A key human-curated data source rejected LLM authorship, which raises the value of verified human content and complicates synthetic-data feedback loops.
insights.locator: Already in 2018 Google was training AI

insights.claim: The 'Death of Wikipedia' argument predicts a downward spiral where fewer human contributors invite more AI replacement, leaving humans relegated to formatting and cleanup of machine text.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Illustrates the broader risk that automation intended for housekeeping displaces creative work and degrades the corpus.

insights.claim: Google's AI Overviews quickly became as central to the search experience as Wikipedia was, while Wikipedia still serves as a source one step removed; if Wikipedia itself becomes AI-corrupted, there is no means of proving the AI wrong.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: AI answers depend on a reliable human reference layer; its degradation raises hallucination verification risk.

insights.claim: The author argues AGI would be both the culmination and end of encyclopedias, with human-written ones surviving only as secular scriptures in the mind of a digital god.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: The AGI narrative is framed as a revival of the Enlightenment ambition for a single all-knowing authority.
insights.quote: secular scriptures in the mind of a digital god

insights.claim: The author warns that a single machine-edited encyclopedia acting as final authority would be cold and monotonous 'slop', and that nothing guarantees an AI encyclopedia would be unifying.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Centralized AI knowledge authorities carry epistemic and governance risk that may drive regulation and demand for pluralistic sources.
insights.locator: Implicit in the idea of a single, machine-edited encyclopedia

insights.claim: Wikipedia's lasting value may be its process, the slow human collaboration of people from many nations at Wikimania, rather than its contents.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Suggests the durable moat of human knowledge communities is trust and process, not content that AI can replicate.
insights.locator: The real existing Wikipedia feels less melodramatic

insights.claim: Wikipedia's co-founders diverged: Jimmy Wales stayed an internationalist who criticizes the MAGA movement, while Larry Sanger became a vaccine skeptic, voted for Trump and in 2025 declared himself a Christian, showing the culture-war pressure on knowledge institutions.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Political polarization of the founders reflects why neutrality of the platform faces attack from multiple sides.
insights.locator: The divergent paths of Jimmy Wales

insights.claim: Past encyclopedias from the Great Soviet Encyclopedia to the Enciclopedia Italiana expressed nationalist and totalitarian intent, and H. G. Wells assumed his World Brain would empower a world government that, if all-knowing, would be repressive.
insights.speaker: Richard Cooke
insights.so_what: Centralized knowledge systems have historically been tools of power, a lens for judging AI-controlled knowledge.
insights.locator: Less obvious to us now is that World Brain
